title: Audit event contract evolution - draft
content:
Purpose:
This draft describes a proposed evolution of the Redwood audit event contract to support RBAC v2, more explicit evidence automation hooks, and a SIEM-friendly export mapping. It is intended as a pragmatic migration path that preserves backwards compat where possible, identifies breaking changes, and gives implementers a step-by-step rollout checklist.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- Provide a deterministic, typed audit event shape usable by analytics, incident response, and compliance exports.
- Enable RBAC v2 attributes to be captured with minimal runtime overhead.
- Surface evidence references (artifact pointers) so evidence automation can collect consistent artifacts (logs, snapshots, policy diffs).
- Normalize fields for straightforward SIEM/ELK/ECS transformation while retaining Redwood-specific fields.
- Version the contract to allow future additive changes without breaking downstream consumers.

Design principles:
1) Single canonical event: one authoritative JSON sent to internal audit topics; other consumers transform or filter.
2) Namespaced, stable keyset: core fields are stable; extensions live in a single "extensions" map prefixed by component.
3) Differentiation between identity and principal metadata: clearly separate actor identity (who authenticated) from principal (policy principal that was evaluated).
4) Evidence-by-reference: large artifacts are referenced (S3/KV pointers) not inlined to keep events small.
5) Explicit contract versions: every event must include "contract_version" and a human-readable "schema_ref" when non-default.

Event model (high level):
- envelope: metadata about transport and schema: {"contract_version","event_id","created_at","source"}
- actor: who initiated the action: {"actor.id","actor.type","actor.identity_source","actor.auth_method"}
- principal: RBAC evaluation result: {"rbac.principal_id","rbac.principal_type","rbac.role_ids","rbac.policy_snapshot_ref","rbac.decision"}
- resource: target of the action: {"resource.type","resource.id","resource.fingerprint_sha256","resource.labels"}
- action: what occurred: {"action.type","action.verb","action.name","action.parameters"}
- outcome: {"outcome.status","outcome.code","outcome.reason"}
- evidence_refs: array of artifact pointers (signed URLs or internal object ids)
- routing: operational metadata for export/retention: {"sensitivity","retention_tier","siem_exportable"}
- extensions: map of component-specific extra data (warnings: consumer should ignore unknown extension keys)

Core field catalog (consumer-facing names):
- contract_version (string) - required. Semantic versioning: "v2.0" etc.
- event_id (string, uuid) - required.
- created_at (RFC3339 timestamp) - required.
- source (string) - required. E.g., "hosted-api", "dedicated-gpu", "console".
- actor.id (string) - unique principal identifier (immutable where possible).
- actor.type (enum string) - "human" | "service" | "key".
- actor.identity_source (string) - SSO provider or token type: "okta", "api_key", "internal-bearer".
- actor.auth_method (string, optional) - e.g., "mfa", "key-rotate".
- rbac.principal_id (string) - principal used for evaluation (can be different from actor.id).
- rbac.role_ids (array of strings) - canonical role ids evaluated.
- rbac.decision (enum) - "allow" | "deny" | "conditional".
- rbac.policy_snapshot_ref (string) - evidence pointer to the exact policy blob used for decision.
- resource.type (string) - e.g., "model", "deployment", "console-route".
- resource.id (string) - opaque id.
- resource.fingerprint_sha256 (string) - SHA256 of canonical resource descriptor for integrity checks.
- action.type (string) - higher-level classification: "config.change", "generate", "access", "data.read", "data.write".
- action.name (string) - concrete operation: "update_deployment_config".
- action.parameters (object serialized-as-string) - small parameter bag; large inputs must be referenced via evidence_refs.
- outcome.status (string) - "success" | "failure" | "throttled".
- outcome.code (short string) - internal code for classification (e.g., AUTH_DENY_POLICY_03).
- evidence_refs (array of strings) - URIs pointing to artifacts for automation. Acceptable URI schemes: s3://, gs://, redwood://evidence/…
- sensitivity (string) - "low" | "medium" | "high" - used by export and retention policies.
- retention_tier (string) - mapping for lifecycle: "30d-hot", "365d-cold", "archive-7y".

Example (compact, illustrative) - consumer parsers should treat this as example only:
{
  "contract_version": "v2.0",
  "event_id": "4f9a8b2c-7d3e-4caa-9b0d-5a2f0c1b2d3e",
  "created_at": "2026-01-18T14:23:10Z",
  "source": "hosted-api",
  "actor.id": "user:ava.chen@redwood.ai",
  "actor.type": "human",
  "actor.identity_source": "okta",
  "rbac.principal_id": "principal:team-api-prod",
  "rbac.role_ids": ["role:deploy_admin","role:read_logs"],
  "rbac.decision": "allow",
  "rbac.policy_snapshot_ref": "s3://evidence/policy-snapshots/pol-20260118-1.json",
  "resource.type": "deployment",
  "resource.id": "dep-87ac4",
  "resource.fingerprint_sha256": "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb924...",
  "action.type": "config.change",
  "action.name": "update_deployment_config",
  "action.parameters": "{\"scaling.min\":2,\"scaling.max\":8}",
  "outcome.status": "success",
  "evidence_refs": ["s3://evidence/console-screenshots/ev-123.png","redwood://evidence/trace/trace-987"]
}

Versioning and migration notes (v1 -> v2 -> v3):
- v1: initial opportunistic capture. Many fields freeform, inconsistent identity naming, inlined large artifacts, no explicit RBAC principal capture.
- v2 (current draft recommended baseline): Adds contract_version, actor.identity_source, rbac.* namespace, evidence_refs-by-reference, sensitivity & retention_tier. Backwards compatibility: most v1 parsers will continue to work if they tolerate unknown keys, but consumers that assumed inlined artifacts will need migration.
- v3 (future): aim to add typed enums for action.type, standardized parameter schemas per action.name, and optional signed event envelopes for cross-account export. Plan for v3 includes a deprecation window and automated migration tests.
Breaking changes between v1->v2 to watch for:
- removal of inlined large artifacts: consumers must be updated to dereference evidence_refs.
- actor identifier canonicalization: previously free text names will be replaced by canonical ids (user:..., service:...).

RBAC v2 integration guidance:
- When evaluating a policy, emit two events: (1) pre-evaluate (optional) with evaluation inputs (sensitivity: low), and (2) post-evaluate (mandatory) with rbac.decision and rbac.policy_snapshot_ref. The post-evaluate event is the authoritative log for audit.
- rbac.principal_id should be the exact principal (team, service, application) used for evaluation so that lateral-move analysis can be performed.
- policy_snapshot_ref must be deterministically generated and stored to evidence storage with a retention tag matching the event's retention_tier.

SIEM export mapping (recommended normalization layer):
- Map core fields to a lightweight ECS-friendly shape during export to the SIEM pipeline. Example mappings: 
  - event.id <= event_id
  - event.created <= created_at
  - user.name <= actor.id
  - user.domain <= actor.identity_source
  - subject.role_ids <= rbac.role_ids (string-join)
  - rule.name <= rbac.policy_snapshot_ref (strip bucket prefix for index-size savings)
  - file.hash <= resource.fingerprint_sha256 (when resource.type == "artifact")
  - message <= action.name + " " + outcome.code
Notes: keep the original event JSON in a cold store; SIEM index should use a trimmed, searchable subset with a canonical mapping document checked into github for auditability.

Evidence automation hooks (how external automation should consume events):
- Evidence collectors subscribe to the canonical audit topic. When an event with evidence_refs is observed, collectors should: 
  1) verify event.contract_version and reject events older than a configured minimum
  2) fetch policy_snapshot_ref if present and index its content
  3) fetch any artifact URIs that match a configured sensitivity threshold (e.g., high sensitivity fetch immediately, medium fetch on-demand)
  4) create a forensic bundle: {event_id, evidence_refs_fetched, checksums, fetch_timestamps} and store an index entry pointing to the bundle for fast lookup by IR teams
- Collectors must sign fetch operations into their own internal audit chain (collector_id, fetch_time, fetch_status) for traceability.

Validation, tests and rollout plan:
- Schema: produce a JSON Schema (separate repo) and a lightweight validator embedded in the audit producer library.
- Golden tests: unit test producers produce sample events that get validated by integration tests with the ingestion pipeline.
- Backfill: for backward compat, run a migration job that scans v1 events and populates lightweight canonical fields where possible (e.g., set contract_version: v1-migrated).
- Canary rollout: enable new contract version emission in one region or one small service first (e.g., console change flows). Monitor parser errors, SIEM ingestion failures, and IR tool regressions for 72 hours before wider rollout.

Operational considerations and quotas:
- Event size target: target < 4KB per canonical event; evidence_refs can reference larger artifacts.
- Topic partitioning: route events by source and sensitivity to allow consumer teams to opt-in.
- Retention enforcement: retention_tier should drive lifecycle jobs; auditors may request extended retention for specific event_ids (add request workflow).

Open questions (for next review):
- Should action.parameters be converted to typed sub-schemas per action.name in v3? Tradeoff: richer analysis vs schema proliferation.
- How do we index policy snapshots to enable fast lookup for IR without storing full policy in SIEM?
- Should we require signed URIs for evidence_refs for cross-account export?

Next steps / action items:
- Owners: Morgan Patel (schema lead), Priya Nair (RBAC integration), Diego Rivera (evidence automation), Ava Chen (SIEM mapping).
- Short-term (2 weeks): produce machine-readable JSON Schema, a set of 10 golden examples, and a small producer library update to emit contract_version and evidence_refs.
- Medium-term (6–10 weeks): run canary emitters in beta region, create SIEM mapping config, and implement collector fetch signing.
- Long-term (quarter): prototype v3 typed action.params and evaluate signed envelopes for cross-account export.

Appendix: quick migration checklist for integrators:
1) Accept unknown keys in parsers.
2) Update any logic that expects inlined artifacts to follow evidence_refs.
3) Map actor names to canonical ids (team will provide a canonicalization table).
4) Wire up retention_tier mapping to your lifecycle job.
5) Add contract_version checks and alert if older-than-supported versions appear.

Revision history:
- 2025-12-15: initial draft authored (v2.0 proposal)
- 2026-01-08: added SIEM mapping recommendations and evidence automation flow
- 2026-01-20: updated examples and canary rollout section per security review

End of draft.
